analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | prime | FOMC | Brazil | E&Cs | ACCV
key_insights: Brazil's presidential runoff was won by Lula (PT) with 51.8% of valid votes over Flavio Bolsonaro, defying polls. The desk expects the outcome to weigh on Brazilian markets, with IBOV set to open lower.
French assets rallied after the country avoided a ratings downgrade despite protests and violence over the weekend. Germany and France equities were up 70-80bps.
US S&P futures were up 30bps pre-market. KOSPI fell 146bps and Japan fell 80bps. German IFO was 90.2 vs 89.9 survey and 89.9 prior.
WTI fell 200bps to $101 and Brent was $115. European gas rose 250bps to $96, another all-time high. The 10-year yield is below 5%, the dollar is flat and Bitcoin is about $80.4k.
The week brings PCE, the Fed, big tech earnings, and over half of the industrials/materials sector reporting.
Fanuc EBIT was 15% ahead of the Street, with raised guidance and 49% order growth.
CX reported Q3 EBITDA of $990mm vs $953mm consensus on revenue of $4.59bn vs $4.45bn consensus. It maintained full-year guidance and says it is operating ahead of 2027 targets year to date.
GS economists expect the FOMC to raise rates every other meeting. That means skipping a hike at the October meeting and likely hiking in December. The market prices four hikes.

The tightening in broad financial conditions since September is only a bit more than is usually associated with one hike and much less than with four, so the FOMC is unlikely to see it as excessive or a replacement for hikes.

The key October FOMC question is how the statement sentence on the September hike changes. GS thinks it may adapt Vice Chair Jefferson's language that further adjustments will depend on trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. No significant new information is expected from the press conference.

GS does not expect a March 2027 hike because it expects inflation to improve as the effects of tariffs, the energy shock and AI price pressures diminish. A March hike is possible if inflation is worse than expected. The main risk is oil futures above GS forecasts on potential further conflict with Iran, and a larger 'January effect' in price increases.

Market pricing of the Fed path has removed one hike and now peaks at just over 4.5%. GS's baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are considerably less hawkish, since GS doubts four hikes and expects cuts down the road.

Prime: Industrials was among the most net sold US sectors. Hedge funds net sold the sector for a 2nd straight week (7 of the last 8) at the fastest pace in more than 6 months (-1.8 SDs vs 1 year), driven by long-and-short sales (2.5 to 1).

Most net sold subsectors: Ground Transportation, Electrical Equip, Trading Companies & Distributors and Construction & Engineering. Most net bought: Aerospace & Defense, with Airlines, Professional Svcs and Air Freight & Logistics seeing short covers.
Industrials gross/net allocations are 13.2%/11.4% of the US Prime book. The US Industrials long/short ratio is 1.67, in the 2nd percentile vs the past year and the 7th vs three years.

GS (Joe Ritchie) initiated Accelevation (ACCV) at Buy with a $22 price target, based on 13.0x Q5-Q8 EBITDA. ACCV is a vertically integrated maker and installer of modular data center white space and power infrastructure serving hyperscalers, colocation providers and AI data centers.

GS expects ACCV to be the fastest-growing company in its coverage over the next three years (+74%), compounding EBITDA at 77%. ACCV has a $1.1bn backlog and is the basis-of-design for at least three major hyperscalers.

market_movers.rationale: Modular data center white space niche with end-to-end platform, $1.1bn backlog, basis-of-design for at least three hyperscalers. GS expects +74% growth and 77% EBITDA compounding over three years.

tension_points.bull_case: The market prices four hikes with a path peaking at just over 4.5%. FOMC participants appear to support hiking every other meeting, with a high bar to deviate through year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: GS is skeptical of four hikes and expects cuts down the road. It expects inflation to improve as tariff, energy shock and AI price effects diminish, and some participants may prefer to limit the cycle's size.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil futures above GS forecasts on Iran conflict, or worse inflation data, would make a March hike possible. Growth or employment concerns would end the hikes.
